title: Publish thin npm bootstrapper and per-platform packages
notes: This checkout already carried a prior, incomplete pass at this task (commits e32ff24b 'feat(distribution): add fail-closed npm bootstrap contract' and f0ac76de 'feat(distribution): add MCP Registry source metadata', both landed before MBR-903 in this branch's history, neither using the MBR-906 commit-message convention or writing task evidence): npm/index.mjs (PLATFORM_PACKAGES registry, selectPlatform, verifyArtifact, bootstrap), npm/package.json, tests/npm/bootstrap.test.mjs, and docs/install-npm.md's original text. None of those four files were modified by this task except docs/install-npm.md, which was extended (not rewritten) and npm/package.json, which gained bin/optionalDependencies/files additions on top of its existing fields -- verified by re-running the pre-existing tests/npm/bootstrap.test.mjs unchanged (see commands.log; all 5 of its tests still pass alongside this task's new tests).

That prior pass built the generic verify-then-dispatch primitive (bootstrap/selectPlatform/verifyArtifact) but left two things this task's owner instructions explicitly named as gaps: (1) no actual per-platform npm packages existed for PLATFORM_PACKAGES' six registry names, so 'npm i resolves the right binary' had nothing to resolve to; (2) nothing tied the bootstrapper to MBR-903's release pipeline output, so there was no way to learn which platform's artifact MBR-903 had actually verified. This task adds exactly those two pieces, plus the one CLI entry point ('npx install') the acceptance criterion names, all additive on top of the unmodified npm/index.mjs.

npm/platforms/<key>/package.json (six files, one per PLATFORM_PACKAGES entry: darwin-arm64, darwin-x64, linux-arm64, linux-x64, win32-arm64, win32-x64) are real, minimal package manifests with the exact registered name and valid npm os/cpu constraint fields, so npm's own optionalDependency resolution -- the same mechanism esbuild/swc/napi-rs packages use -- installs only the one matching the current host. None declares a 'main', 'files', or bundled binary: no native artifact has been built or signed anywhere in this task's dependency chain, so embedding one would be a fabricated binary, which the hard rules and the notes already in npm/index.mjs explicitly forbid ('this task resolves and fetches, it does not ship binaries'). npm/package.json now lists all six as optionalDependencies and adds a 'bin' entry for npm/bin/membrane.mjs (added to 'files' alongside the pre-existing index.mjs/package.json).

linux-arm64 and linux-x64 are permanent, declared placeholders, not temporary gaps: release/contracts/platforms.v1.json (MBR-903) defines no Linux release target at all, so no RightKit build will ever populate them through this pipeline -- documented in both docs/install-npm.md and scripts/release/npm/resolve-platform-artifacts.mjs's NPM_PLATFORM_TO_PIPELINE_TARGET map (null entries). darwin-x64 and windows-arm64 map to real MBR-903 pipeline targets that scripts/release/pipeline/platform-targets.mjs (unmodified, imported read-only) already marks not-buildable/conformance-only today -- real gaps in apps/membrane-hub's packaging config, outside this task's allowed paths.

scripts/release/npm/resolve-platform-artifacts.mjs is the new, repo-side (never published -- outside npm/package.json's 'files') resolver the task brief explicitly asked for: 'the bootstrapper must resolve the artifacts that pipeline identifies.' It reads MBR-903's immutable evidence/releases/<releaseId>/release-generation.json (written by scripts/release/pipeline/multi-platform-release.mjs --write, imported read-only for its releaseId() naming convention, never re-implemented or modified) and returns, for a target MBR-903 already marked 'verified', the exact {name, sha256} it recorded -- copied verbatim, never re-derived. For every other real state (no release-generation recorded yet, 'pending', 'not-buildable', or no pipeline target at all) it throws a named error (ArtifactNotVerifiedError / NoPipelineTargetError) carrying the real status/reason, never a fabricated artifact. resolveAllNpmPlatformArtifacts runs all six platform keys and never throws itself, returning one {ok, ...} record per key.

Proven directly against this actual, live checkout, not just synthetic fixtures: scripts/release/npm/resolve-platform-artifacts.test.mjs's 'today's real Membrane checkout has no release-generation recorded for a plausible release: nothing is invented' test calls readReleaseGeneration and resolveNpmPlatformArtifact against the real repo root (fileURLToPath-derived, not a temp dir) and asserts null / ArtifactNotVerifiedError -- true today because only macOS builds are sealed under .right-release/sealed/ (six real membrane-hub-*/mac releases exist there) and MBR-903's evidence/releases/**/release-generation.json write-once layer has not been run with --write for any of them yet (only a pre-existing, differently-schemaed evidence/releases/membrane-hub-0.1.1-53efa898/windows.json exists, from an older evidence pipeline, not MBR-903's schema).

npm/bin/membrane.mjs is the new CLI entry point ('npx @orthic/membrane install') the acceptance criterion names. It calls selectPlatform to find the optionalDependency package name npm already selected for this host, dynamically imports it exactly once, requires it to export {artifact, metadata, dispatch}, then reuses the already-loaded instance for npm/index.mjs's existing bootstrap() digest+signature verification (no second real import). Every failure mode is a distinct, named, fail-closed error: UnsupportedPlatformError (host tuple), PlatformPackageMissingError (platform package not installed, or installed but missing its verified export), ArtifactVerificationError (digest or signature mismatch -- the acceptance criterion's 'rejects a checksum/signature mismatch', demonstrated at the CLI layer, not only the library layer), and SigningTrustNotConfiguredError (the default verifySignature, used when no caller supplies a trust root, throws rather than fabricating trust -- this package ships no signing public key; that is MBR-901/MBR-902/MBR-911's release-gate territory, outside this task's allowlist).

tests/npm/install-cli.test.mjs (7 tests) proves the full acceptance path deterministically with no network or registry access: a correctly signed, matching-digest fixture verifies and dispatches (asserting the platform package is imported exactly once, then reused); unsupported host tuples fail closed before any package load is attempted; a missing platform package and one missing artifact/metadata both fail closed as PlatformPackageMissingError; digest mismatch and signature-verification failure both reject as ArtifactVerificationError before dispatch is ever called (asserted via a `dispatched` flag that stays false); and the default verifySignature (no caller override) fails closed as SigningTrustNotConfiguredError. tests/npm/platform-packages.test.mjs (4 tests) proves the six npm/platforms/** scaffolds stay in lockstep with npm/index.mjs's PLATFORM_PACKAGES registry (names, os/cpu fields, semver-valid versions), that none declares a bundled binary, and that npm/package.json's optionalDependencies and files fields are correct.

No cargo, pnpm, Tauri, right-release, npm publish, codesign, notarytool, stapler, spctl, signtool, or AzureSignTool command was run at any point. No mutating git command (add/commit/checkout/stash/reset/rebase/push) was run. Only `node --test tests/npm/*.test.mjs scripts/release/npm/*.test.mjs` was executed (23/23 pass -- see commands.log), covering this task's four new test files plus the pre-existing tests/npm/bootstrap.test.mjs unchanged. No .github/workflows/**, CI, or hosted/self-hosted runner configuration was added.

Root package.json was deliberately left unmodified: nothing this task needed required a root-level change (the pre-existing 'test' script is explicitly owned by a separate, later change per this task's hard rules, and this task's new tests are discoverable directly via `node --test tests/npm/*.test.mjs scripts/release/npm/*.test.mjs` without touching it).
